programme.displayName: CloudFront: Secure S3 Content Delivery Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Secure, customize, observe, and remove CloudFront delivery from a private Amazon S3 origin
programme.description: An intermediate CloudFront lab using a private Amazon S3 origin in eu-west-2. You create two dedicated buckets, deliver protected content through CloudFront using origin access control (OAC), apply cache and security-header behavior, add a CloudFront Function, enable standard logging, test invalidation and metrics, and remove every lab resource.
programme.learningOutcome: Build and operate a secure CloudFront distribution that serves content from a private S3 bucket; explain OAC, cache keys, managed cache policies, response headers policies, CloudFront Functions, logging, metrics, invalidations, and safe reverse-dependency cleanup.

tasks.title: Create the private content and log buckets
tasks.feature: Amazon S3 origins and logging destinations
tasks.goal: Create dedicated content and log buckets in eu-west-2, keep both buckets non-public, prepare the log bucket for CloudFront standard logging, and upload index.html plus assets/site.css to the content bucket.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudFront should retrieve origin objects through an origin access control (OAC), not through public S3 permissions. Separating content from access logs makes access control, retention, and final cleanup clearer.

consoleSteps.title: Record training values and create the local website files
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ In the AWS Management Console navigation bar, choose your account name.

instructions.text: ☐ In the AWS Management Console navigation bar, choose your account name.
☐ Copy the 12-digit Account ID and record it as <ACCOUNT_ID>.
☐ On your computer, create an empty folder named cloudfront-secure-content-lab.
☐ In that folder, create a file named index.html.
☐ In assets, create a file named site.css.
☐ Copy the exact contents from the two file blocks into their matching files and save both files.

☐ Use cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> as the content-bucket name and cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> as the log-bucket name. <ACCOUNT_ID> means the 12-digit value you recorded, not the literal placeholder.

jsonBlocks.title: Save as cloudfront-secure-content-lab/index.html
jsonBlocks.content:
CloudFront secure content lab

Delivered from a private Amazon S3 origin through CloudFront.

jsonBlocks.title: Save as cloudfront-secure-content-lab/assets/site.css
jsonBlocks.content:
body { font-family: sans-serif; margin: 3rem; color: #0f172a; }
h1 { color: #0891b2; }

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The local cloudfront-secure-content-lab folder contains index.html and assets/site.css.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not put secrets, access keys, or confidential content in either training file.

consoleSteps.title: Create and inspect the private content bucket

instructions.text: ☐ In AWS Region, choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
☐ Leave Block all public access selected.
☐ In General purpose buckets, open cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
☐ In Block public access (Bucket settings), confirm that Block all public access is On.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The content bucket exists in eu-west-2 and its bucket-level public-access block is enabled.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not select an S3 website hosting endpoint or disable public access blocking for this origin bucket.

consoleSteps.title: Create and inspect the private log bucket
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Return to General purpose buckets and choose Create bucket.

instructions.text: ☐ Return to General purpose buckets and choose Create bucket.
☐ In AWS Region, choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
☐ Leave Block all public access selected.

☐ Under Object Ownership, choose the setting required by the Standard logging page if the console reports that ACLs must be enabled for the selected logging mode; otherwise retain the secure default shown by the console.
☐ In Block public access (Bucket settings), confirm that Block all public access is On.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The dedicated log bucket exists in eu-west-2, is not publicly readable, and is ready for the CloudFront standard-logging workflow.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudFront logging requirements differ by logging mode and account configuration. Follow any visible S3 ownership or ACL requirement presented by the CloudFront logging workflow; do not make the bucket public.

consoleSteps.title: Upload the supplied website files

instructions.text: ☐ Choose Add files and select cloudfront-secure-content-lab/index.html.
☐ Choose Add folder and select cloudfront-secure-content-lab/assets.
☐ After upload completes, confirm that index.html and the assets/ prefix appear in the Objects list.
☐ Open assets/ and confirm that site.css appears.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The content bucket contains exactly the training objects index.html and assets/site.css.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not apply a public object ACL or public bucket policy.

cliSteps.command:
mkdir -p cloudfront-secure-content-lab/assets cat > cloudfront-secure-content-lab/index.html <<'EOF' CloudFront secure content lab

CloudFront secure content lab

Delivered from a private Amazon S3 origin through CloudFront.

EOF cat > cloudfront-secure-content-lab/assets/site.css <<'EOF' body { font-family: sans-serif; margin: 3rem; color: #0f172a; } h1 { color: #0891b2; } EOF
cliSteps.explanation: Run this in a local terminal. It creates the exact two non-sensitive files required by this CLI route. Replace <LAB_PROFILE> in later commands with the name of your already configured, authorized AWS CLI profile; it is not an AWS resource created by this task.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local folder contains index.html and assets/site.css.
cliSteps.warning: Use an authorized non-root profile. Do not store credentials in these files.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the 12-digit account ID and <LAB_PROFILE> with your local CLI profile name. Record the bucket name exactly; later tasks use it as the S3 origin.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a Location for cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
cliSteps.warning: Bucket names are globally unique. Stop and choose a different account-specific training name only if S3 reports that the name is unavailable.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: This applies all four bucket-level public-access-block controls to the content bucket.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds without output.
cliSteps.warning: OAC, created later, supplies the required CloudFront-to-S3 read path; public access is not required.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the separate log destination. Before enabling CloudFront logging in task 4, check the current logging workflow for any required bucket ownership or ACL setting.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a Location for cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
cliSteps.warning: Keep logs separate from origin objects because logs can contain request metadata.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: This applies all four public-access-block controls to the log bucket.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds without output.
cliSteps.warning: Public-access block does not itself configure CloudFront log delivery.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp cloudfront-secure-content-lab/index.html s3://cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/index.html --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Upload the local file created in the first CLI step to the exact default-root-object key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The CLI reports an upload to s3://cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/index.html.
cliSteps.warning: Run this from the directory containing cloudfront-secure-content-lab.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp cloudfront-secure-content-lab/assets/site.css s3://cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/assets/site.css --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Upload the stylesheet with the assets/site.css key referenced by index.html.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The CLI reports an upload to s3://cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/assets/site.css.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use --acl public-read.

verification.title: Verify the exact private-origin objects
verification.instruction: In the S3 console, open cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>, then open Objects and assets/.

verification.title: Verify both public-access-block resources
verification.instruction: Run get-public-access-block for each named bucket, or inspect each bucket's Permissions tab.
verification.expectedResult: Each bucket shows BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, and RestrictPublicBuckets enabled.

tasks.title: Create an OAC-protected distribution
tasks.goal: Create cf-secure-content-lab-oac, create a CloudFront distribution whose default root object is index.html, then add the exact distribution-scoped S3 bucket policy that permits CloudFront reads.
tasks.whyItMatters: OAC signs CloudFront requests to the S3 origin. The S3 bucket remains private because the bucket policy permits only the CloudFront service principal and only the ARN of this distribution.

consoleSteps.title: Create the distribution and OAC from the S3 origin workflow

instructions.text: ☐ Select the website or application distribution option shown by the console, then choose Next.
☐ Choose Browse S3 and select cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
☐ Confirm that Origin access control is enabled or that an OAC named cf-secure-content-lab-oac is offered; create it if the console asks for an OAC name.
☐ In Default root object, enter index.html.
☐ Keep the viewer protocol policy shown by the recommended secure configuration.
☐ Open the created distribution and record its Distribution ID as [DISTRIBUTION_ID], domain name as [DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN_NAME], and ARN as [DISTRIBUTION_ARN].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A distribution is created with the private S3 bucket as its origin and an OAC-backed origin configuration.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not select an S3 website endpoint. Website endpoints cannot use OAC.

consoleSteps.title: Install and inspect the exact origin bucket policy
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Open the S3 console and open cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.

instructions.text: ☐ Open the S3 console and open cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
☐ Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> and [DISTRIBUTION_ID] in the supplied policy. <ACCOUNT_ID> is the 12-digit account ID from task 1; [DISTRIBUTION_ID] is the value recorded in the preceding step.
☐ Replace the entire policy editor content with the supplied policy.
☐ Confirm that the Bucket policy section displays the saved policy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The content bucket has the CloudFrontReadOnlyOAC policy and no public-read statement.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use Principal "*" and do not change the condition to another distribution ARN.

consoleSteps.title: Wait for deployment and test the protected path

instructions.text: ☐ Wait until the Last modified/deployment state is complete and the distribution is enabled.
☐ In a private browser window, try the direct S3 object URL for index.html.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudFront serves the page while direct unauthenticated S3 access is denied.
consoleSteps.warning: Distribution deployment is asynchronous and can take several minutes.

cliSteps.command:
cat > oac-config.json <<'EOF'
{
  "Name": "cf-secure-content-lab-oac",
  "Description": "OAC for cf-secure-content-lab private S3 origin",
  "SigningProtocol": "sigv4",
  "SigningBehavior": "always",
  "OriginAccessControlOriginType": "s3"
}
EOF
aws cloudfront create-origin-access-control --origin-access-control-config file://oac-config.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Save the complete OAC document as oac-config.json in the current terminal directory, then run the command. Record OriginAccessControl.Id as [OAC_ID] and the returned ETag as [OAC_ETAG]. CloudFront commands are global, so no --region is used.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an OAC named cf-secure-content-lab-oac in the created configuration.
cliSteps.warning: Use the same <LAB_PROFILE> as task 1. Do not substitute an origin access identity for this OAC lab.

cliSteps.command:
cat > distribution-config.json <<'EOF'
{
  "CallerReference": "cf-secure-content-lab-<UNIQUE_VALUE>",
  "Comment": "CloudFront secure S3 content training distribution",
  "Enabled": true,
  "DefaultRootObject": "index.html",
  "Origins": {
    "Quantity": 1,
    "Items": [
      {
        "Id": "content-s3-origin",
        "DomainName": "cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com",
        "OriginAccessControlId": "[OAC_ID]",
        "S3OriginConfig": {"OriginAccessIdentity": ""}
      }
    ]
  },
  "DefaultCacheBehavior": {
    "TargetOriginId": "content-s3-origin",
    "ViewerProtocolPolicy": "redirect-to-https",
    "AllowedMethods": {"Quantity": 2, "Items": ["GET", "HEAD"], "CachedMethods": {"Quantity": 2, "Items": ["GET", "HEAD"]}},
    "Compress": true,
    "TrustedSigners": {"Enabled": false, "Quantity": 0},
    "TrustedKeyGroups": {"Enabled": false, "Quantity": 0},
    "ForwardedValues": {"QueryString": false, "Cookies": {"Forward": "none"}, "Headers": {"Quantity": 0}, "QueryStringCacheKeys": {"Quantity": 0}},
    "MinTTL": 0
  },
  "CacheBehaviors": {"Quantity": 0},
  "CustomErrorResponses": {"Quantity": 0},
  "Restrictions": {"GeoRestriction": {"RestrictionType": "none", "Quantity": 0}},
  "ViewerCertificate": {"CloudFrontDefaultCertificate": true},
  "HttpVersion": "http2",
  "IsIPV6Enabled": true
}
EOF
cliSteps.explanation: Create distribution-config.json in the current directory. Replace <ACCOUNT_ID>, [OAC_ID], and <UNIQUE_VALUE> before continuing. <UNIQUE_VALUE> must be a value not reused by another distribution creation, for example your current UTC timestamp. Do not change it after the create call.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A complete distribution configuration file exists locally.
cliSteps.warning: This file deliberately uses the regional S3 REST endpoint, not an S3 website endpoint.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront create-distribution --distribution-config file://distribution-config.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Create the global CloudFront distribution. Record Distribution.Id as [DISTRIBUTION_ID], Distribution.DomainName as [DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN_NAME], Distribution.ARN as [DISTRIBUTION_ARN], and ETag as [DISTRIBUTION_ETAG].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows Status InProgress and includes the four recorded values.
cliSteps.warning: The origin is not readable until the next step adds the distribution-specific S3 policy.

cliSteps.explanation: Save the policy, replace <ACCOUNT_ID> and [DISTRIBUTION_ARN] with the recorded values from the preceding command, then apply it. This creates the inventory resource named CloudFrontReadOnlyOAC policy on cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output and the bucket policy exists.
cliSteps.warning: This grants read access only to the exact distribution ARN; it is not a public bucket policy.

verification.title: Verify OAC and policy scope
verification.instruction: Inspect the CloudFront origin configuration and the content bucket policy.
verification.expectedResult: The origin has an OAC and the policy principal is cloudfront.amazonaws.com with AWS:SourceArn equal to [DISTRIBUTION_ARN].

verification.title: Verify delivery without public S3 access
verification.instruction: After deployment completes, request https://[DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN_NAME]/index.html and then request the direct S3 object URL anonymously.
verification.expectedResult: CloudFront returns the page and direct S3 access is denied.

tasks.title: Apply cache and response-header controls
tasks.feature: CloudFront cache behaviors, invalidations, and response headers policies
tasks.goal: Use the CachingOptimized managed cache policy, add cf-secure-content-lab-security-headers to the default cache behavior, and create the narrow /index.html invalidation.
tasks.whyItMatters: The cache policy controls cache-key and TTL behavior. A response headers policy applies browser-facing security headers consistently at CloudFront. An invalidation is an explicit request to remove a cached path before normal expiry.

consoleSteps.title: Create the response headers policy

instructions.text: ☐ Enable X-Content-Type-Options and leave Override origin selected.
☐ Leave Include subdomains and Preload disabled for this minimal training policy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Response headers policies list contains cf-secure-content-lab-security-headers.
consoleSteps.warning: This small policy is not a complete production browser-security policy.

consoleSteps.title: Associate the managed cache and custom headers policies

instructions.text: ☐ In Response headers policy, choose cf-secure-content-lab-security-headers.
☐ Wait for the distribution deployment to complete.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Default behavior has Managed-CachingOptimized and cf-secure-content-lab-security-headers associated.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add request headers, cookies, or query strings to a cache key unless the origin content truly varies by them.

consoleSteps.title: Create and record the narrow invalidation

instructions.text: ☐ Record the resulting invalidation identifier as [INVALIDATION_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The exact home-page invalidation [INVALIDATION_ID] for /index.html is Completed.
consoleSteps.warning: Invalidations cannot be cancelled after creation.

cliSteps.explanation: Save the complete policy document as security-headers-policy.json, then create it. Record ResponseHeadersPolicy.Id as [RESPONSE_HEADERS_POLICY_ID] and ETag as [RESPONSE_HEADERS_POLICY_ETAG].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies cf-secure-content-lab-security-headers and its policy ID.
cliSteps.warning: CloudFront is global, so no --region is used.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --output json > current-distribution-config-response.json
cliSteps.explanation: This obtains the current ETag and complete deployed configuration. Record the top-level ETag as [DISTRIBUTION_ETAG]. Use the DistributionConfig object, not the whole response, in the update file.
cliSteps.expectedResult: current-distribution-config-response.json contains ETag and DistributionConfig.
cliSteps.warning: Never update a distribution using a stale ETag or a partial configuration.

cliSteps.command:
cat > updated-distribution-config.json <<'EOF'
{
  "CallerReference": "cf-secure-content-lab-<UNIQUE_VALUE>",
  "Comment": "CloudFront secure S3 content training distribution",
  "Enabled": true,
  "DefaultRootObject": "index.html",
  "Origins": {"Quantity": 1, "Items": [{"Id": "content-s3-origin", "DomainName": "cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com", "OriginAccessControlId": "[OAC_ID]", "S3OriginConfig": {"OriginAccessIdentity": ""}}]},
  "DefaultCacheBehavior": {
    "TargetOriginId": "content-s3-origin",
    "ViewerProtocolPolicy": "redirect-to-https",
    "AllowedMethods": {"Quantity": 2, "Items": ["GET", "HEAD"], "CachedMethods": {"Quantity": 2, "Items": ["GET", "HEAD"]}},
    "Compress": true,
    "TrustedSigners": {"Enabled": false, "Quantity": 0},
    "TrustedKeyGroups": {"Enabled": false, "Quantity": 0},
    "CachePolicyId": "658327ea-f89d-4fab-a63d-7e88639e58f6",
    "ResponseHeadersPolicyId": "[RESPONSE_HEADERS_POLICY_ID]"
  },
  "CacheBehaviors": {"Quantity": 0},
  "CustomErrorResponses": {"Quantity": 0},
  "Restrictions": {"GeoRestriction": {"RestrictionType": "none", "Quantity": 0}},
  "ViewerCertificate": {"CloudFrontDefaultCertificate": true},
  "HttpVersion": "http2",
  "IsIPV6Enabled": true
}
EOF
cliSteps.explanation: Save this full configuration file and replace <UNIQUE_VALUE>, <ACCOUNT_ID>, [OAC_ID], and [RESPONSE_HEADERS_POLICY_ID]. <UNIQUE_VALUE>, <ACCOUNT_ID>, and [OAC_ID] are the values used in task 2. The CachingOptimized managed policy ID is fixed in this training configuration. The legacy ForwardedValues and MinTTL fields are intentionally absent because CachePolicyId controls the cache key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A complete update document preserving the origin and OAC while adding cache and response-header policies exists locally.
cliSteps.warning: If your current distribution has additional fields not created by this Follow Along, edit the downloaded DistributionConfig instead and preserve those fields.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront update-distribution --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --if-match [DISTRIBUTION_ETAG] --distribution-config file://updated-distribution-config.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Apply the complete updated configuration. Record the response ETag because later distribution changes require a newer current ETag.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows an InProgress distribution update.
cliSteps.warning: Do not remove OriginAccessControlId while editing the configuration.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --paths /index.html --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Create the exact invalidation path and record Invalidation.Id as [INVALIDATION_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response returns [INVALIDATION_ID] with Status InProgress.
cliSteps.warning: CloudFront is global, so no --region is used.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront wait invalidation-completed --distribution-id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --id [INVALIDATION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Wait for the invalidation created in the preceding step.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns successfully when [INVALIDATION_ID] for /index.html is completed.
cliSteps.warning: Do not create a wildcard invalidation for this small targeted content change.

verification.title: Verify response headers
verification.instruction: Request https://[DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN_NAME]/index.html and inspect its response headers in browser developer tools or with an HTTP client.
verification.expectedResult: The response includes x-content-type-options and strict-transport-security.

verification.title: Verify the exact invalidation resource
verification.instruction: Inspect the distribution Invalidations tab or query [INVALIDATION_ID].
verification.expectedResult: [INVALIDATION_ID] identifies the /index.html invalidation and has Status Completed.

tasks.title: Add an edge redirect and delivery observability
tasks.feature: CloudFront Functions, standard logs, and CloudWatch metrics
tasks.goal: Create and publish cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect, associate its LIVE version with the Default behavior viewer-request event, configure standard logging to cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/cloudfront/, and inspect CloudFront delivery metrics.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudFront Functions can make lightweight viewer-request decisions at edge locations. Standard logs provide request-level records, while CloudWatch metrics provide distribution-level traffic and error signals.

consoleSteps.title: Create and publish the redirect function

instructions.text: ☐ Replace the editor contents with the supplied function code.
☐ Confirm that the function page identifies the LIVE stage.

jsonBlocks.title: Function code for cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The exact resource LIVE stage of cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect exists.
consoleSteps.warning: The function redirects only /. All other URI values are returned unchanged.

consoleSteps.title: Associate the published LIVE function

instructions.text: ☐ In Event type, choose Viewer request.
☐ In Function ARN or name, choose cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The exact Default behavior viewer-request association invokes the published LIVE function.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not associate a DEVELOPMENT-stage function.

consoleSteps.title: Enable and inspect standard logging

instructions.text: ☐ Select cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> as the destination bucket.
☐ If the console reports a bucket ownership or ACL prerequisite, return to the log bucket and apply exactly the setting required by the message before retrying.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The exact standard logging destination is cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/cloudfront/.
consoleSteps.warning: Logs are asynchronous and may contain request metadata. Keep the log bucket private.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect CloudFront metrics

instructions.text: ☐ Inspect Requests, Bytes downloaded, 4xx error rate, and 5xx error rate.
☐ Generate several requests to https://[DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN_NAME]/ and https://[DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN_NAME]/index.html.
☐ Refresh Monitoring after metrics have had time to populate.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You can inspect aggregate request, transfer, and error metrics for the distribution.
consoleSteps.warning: A new low-traffic lab can show sparse or zero values.

cliSteps.explanation: Save the complete function file and create the DEVELOPMENT-stage function. Record the returned ETag as [FUNCTION_ETAG].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect in DEVELOPMENT.
cliSteps.warning: CloudFront is global, so no --region is supplied.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront publish-function --name cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect --if-match [FUNCTION_ETAG] --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Publish the exact saved code. Record the returned FunctionSummary.FunctionMetadata.FunctionARN as [LIVE_FUNCTION_ARN] and record the returned ETag as [LIVE_FUNCTION_ETAG].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies the LIVE stage of cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect.
cliSteps.warning: A stale function ETag causes publication to fail.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --output json > function-current-config.json
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned top-level ETag as [FUNCTION_ASSOCIATION_ETAG]. Use the current DistributionConfig as the basis for the next update so the OAC, cache policy, and response headers policy remain intact.
cliSteps.expectedResult: function-current-config.json contains the current ETag and complete configuration.
cliSteps.warning: Do not reuse the ETag from task 3 after a deployment update.

cliSteps.command:
Create function-association-distribution-config.json by copying the current DistributionConfig and adding this exact object under DefaultCacheBehavior:
"FunctionAssociations": {"Quantity": 1, "Items": [{"FunctionARN": "[LIVE_FUNCTION_ARN]", "EventType": "viewer-request"}]}
Then run:
aws cloudfront update-distribution --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --if-match [FUNCTION_ASSOCIATION_ETAG] --distribution-config file://function-association-distribution-config.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: The supplied object is the complete new FunctionAssociations value. [LIVE_FUNCTION_ARN] comes from publish-function. Preserve every other field from function-current-config.json, including the OAC origin, CachePolicyId, and ResponseHeadersPolicyId. Record the update response ETag as [LOGGING_ETAG] after the update is accepted.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The distribution update begins and the Default behavior gains the viewer-request association.
cliSteps.warning: A distribution configuration is account-specific; preserve the full current configuration rather than creating a partial document.

cliSteps.command:
After the preceding update is deployed, run:
aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --output json > logging-current-config.json
Copy its DistributionConfig to logging-distribution-config.json and set its Logging object exactly to:
"Logging": {"Enabled": true, "IncludeCookies": false, "Bucket": "cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>.s3.amazonaws.com", "Prefix": "cloudfront/"}
Then record its current ETag as [LOGGING_ETAG] and run:
aws cloudfront update-distribution --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --if-match [LOGGING_ETAG] --distribution-config file://logging-distribution-config.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: This separately creates the exact distribution logging association: Standard logging destination cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/cloudfront/. Preserve the existing FunctionAssociations and all other configuration values when adding Logging.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The update begins with standard logging enabled for the specified bucket and prefix.
cliSteps.warning: If CloudFront rejects the bucket, resolve the ownership or ACL prerequisite using the Standard logging documentation; do not make the bucket public.

tasks.title: Perform final solution checks and reverse-dependency cleanup
tasks.goal: Validate the secure private-origin baseline, then remove every created CloudFront and S3 resource in reverse dependency order, including the exact associations, invalidation history target, policy, public-access-block configurations, and bucket objects.
tasks.whyItMatters: A final review catches accidental public access before deletion. Reverse-dependency cleanup avoids resource-in-use errors and prevents continued charges for CloudFront requests, S3 storage, and retained access logs.

consoleSteps.title: Validate the deployed security baseline
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Open cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> in Amazon S3 and choose Permissions.

instructions.text: ☐ Open cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> in Amazon S3 and choose Permissions.
☐ Confirm Block all public access is enabled.
☐ Open Bucket policy and confirm the policy statement Sid is CloudFrontReadOnlyOAC.
☐ Open [DISTRIBUTION_ID] in CloudFront, then open Behaviors.
☐ Confirm Response headers policy is cf-secure-content-lab-security-headers.
☐ Confirm Function associations contains Viewer request and cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect.
☐ Open General and confirm Standard logging destination is cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/cloudfront/.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The root redirects to index.html, CloudFront serves the page with configured headers, the S3 origin remains private, and the exact logging association is present.
consoleSteps.warning: Complete the cleanup steps immediately after validation unless the environment is intentionally retained.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --output json > cleanup-current-config.json
cliSteps.explanation: Before every distribution update, obtain a fresh current ETag and complete DistributionConfig. The top-level ETag is the value for --if-match; the DistributionConfig object is the file content to edit.
cliSteps.expectedResult: cleanup-current-config.json contains the current ETag and deployed configuration.
cliSteps.warning: CloudFront is global. Never use an old ETag after a distribution update.

cliSteps.command:
Create cleanup-without-associations.json by copying the DistributionConfig from cleanup-current-config.json and making all of these changes in the same document:
1. Set Logging to {"Enabled":false,"IncludeCookies":false,"Bucket":"","Prefix":""}.
2. Set DefaultCacheBehavior.FunctionAssociations to {"Quantity":0}.
3. Remove DefaultCacheBehavior.ResponseHeadersPolicyId.
Then run:
aws cloudfront update-distribution --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --if-match [CURRENT_ETAG] --distribution-config file://cleanup-without-associations.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: This removes exactly three dependent resources in one required distribution update: Standard logging destination cf-secure-logs-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID>/cloudfront/, Default behavior viewer-request association for cf-secure-content-lab-index-redirect, and Default behavior response headers policy association. [CURRENT_ETAG] is the ETag from the preceding get-distribution-config output.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The distribution enters InProgress with logging and both policy/function associations removed.
cliSteps.warning: Preserve the origin, OAC, cache policy, and all unrelated configuration fields.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront get-invalidation --distribution-id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --id [INVALIDATION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Inspect the exact historical invalidation resource [INVALIDATION_ID] for /index.html. CloudFront invalidations have no separate delete operation; its history is removed when the distribution is deleted.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies [INVALIDATION_ID], its /index.html path, and Completed status.
cliSteps.warning: Do not create another invalidation during cleanup.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Remove exactly the CloudFrontReadOnlyOAC policy on cf-secure-content-lab-<ACCOUNT_ID> before disabling and deleting its dependent distribution.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: This intentionally makes CloudFront unable to read the private origin during deletion. Do not remove any unrelated bucket policy.

cliSteps.command:
aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --output json > disable-current-config.json
Create disable-distribution-config.json by copying its DistributionConfig and changing only "Enabled" to false.
aws cloudfront update-distribution --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --if-match [DISABLE_ETAG] --distribution-config file://disable-distribution-config.json --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: [DISABLE_ETAG] is the fresh top-level ETag in disable-current-config.json. This disables the distribution only after its logging, function, headers association, and origin bucket policy have been removed.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The distribution update begins with Enabled set to false.
cliSteps.warning: Wait until the distribution is fully deployed and disabled before attempting deletion.

cliSteps.command:
aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile <LAB_PROFILE> --output json > delete-current-config.json
aws cloudfront delete-distribution --id [DISTRIBUTION_ID] --if-match [DELETE_ETAG] --profile <LAB_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: After the disabled deployment completes, use the fresh ETag in delete-current-config.json as [DELETE_ETAG]. This deletes [DISTRIBUTION_ID], including its invalidation history.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The delete command succeeds and the distribution no longer appears after deletion completes.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete another distribution.

findings.message: The protected source set includes CloudFront distribution creation and update references but does not include the AWS CLI reference pages for create-origin-access-control, delete-origin-access-control, delete-function, delete-response-headers-policy, get-distribution-config, get-function, or get-invalidation. Their CLI commands are included for a complete operational flow but should be reviewed against the current AWS CLI reference before publication.

CloudFront update-distribution requires the full current distribution configuration and current ETag. The CLI routes explicitly obtain these values, but the complete JSON cannot be safely fixed because generated origin IDs, OAC IDs, policy IDs, log settings, and distribution-specific values differ for every learner.

CloudFront standard-log bucket requirements can vary by logging mode and account configuration. Before publication, verify the current console logging workflow and any required S3 ownership or ACL settings against the current Standard logging documentation.
